name: Windows PowerShell Cmdlets
description: Protects against destructive PowerShell cmdlets: registry/provider deletes \ (`Remove-Item HKLM:\`, `Remove-ItemProperty`, `Remove-PSDrive`), account/task \ removal (`Remove-LocalUser`, `Unregister-ScheduledTask`), `Disable-ComputerRestore`, \ forced `Stop-Computer`/`Restart-Computer`, and `Remove-VM`/`Remove-AppxPackage`.

destructive_patterns.name: remove-item-provider
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-Item against a registry/cert/WSMan provider path deletes that store entry.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-Item HKLM:\...` (or `HKCU:`/`Cert:`/`WSMan:`) deletes a registry key, \ certificate, or WSMan config item — not a file. The registry/cert stores have no \ Recycle Bin, and a wrong key can break apps, services, or trust.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-ItemProperty / Get-ChildItem on the path to confirm contents first \ - Export the key (reg export) before removing it

destructive_patterns.name: remove-itemproperty-or-clear
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-ItemProperty / Clear-Item* deletes registry values or item contents.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-ItemProperty` deletes a registry value; `Clear-Item`/`Clear-ItemProperty` wipe an \ item's contents/value. Against the registry these silently remove configuration with no \ undo.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-ItemProperty: read the value first \ - Export the parent key before changing values

destructive_patterns.name: remove-psdrive
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-PSDrive removes a PowerShell drive mapping.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-PSDrive` removes a PowerShell drive. For a persistent or system drive this can \ break scripts and access that depend on it.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-PSDrive: confirm which drive and whether anything relies on it

destructive_patterns.name: remove-localuser-or-group
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-LocalUser / Remove-LocalGroup deletes a local account or group.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-LocalUser`/`Remove-LocalGroup` permanently deletes a local account or group and \ its access. The user's profile/data can be orphaned and there is no undo.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-LocalUser: confirm the account first \ - Disable-LocalUser: disable reversibly instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: unregister-scheduledtask
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Unregister-ScheduledTask` deletes a scheduled task. If maintenance, backups, or apps \ rely on it, that work silently stops running.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-ScheduledTask: confirm the task first \ - Disable-ScheduledTask: disable reversibly instead

destructive_patterns.name: disable-computerrestore
destructive_patterns.description: Disable-ComputerRestore turns off System Restore and discards restore points.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Disable-ComputerRestore` turns off System Restore for a drive and deletes its existing \ restore points — removing a key local recovery path, much like deleting shadow copies.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-ComputerRestorePoint: review existing restore points first \ - Checkpoint-Computer: create a restore point rather than disabling protection

destructive_patterns.name: force-stop-or-restart-computer
destructive_patterns.description: Stop-Computer/Restart-Computer -Force shuts down/reboots without saving work.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Stop-Computer -Force` / `Restart-Computer -Force` powers off or reboots immediately, \ bypassing apps' save/close prompts — unsaved work in any running program is lost, and on \ a server it drops every session.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Drop -Force so applications can save and close cleanly \ - Confirm no critical work/sessions are active before forcing

destructive_patterns.name: remove-vm-or-snapshot
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-VM / Remove-VMSnapshot deletes a virtual machine or its checkpoints.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-VM` deletes a Hyper-V virtual machine's configuration; `Remove-VMSnapshot`/\ `Remove-VMCheckpoint` deletes its checkpoints (a recovery path). Targeting the wrong VM \ destroys it or its ability to roll back.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-VM: confirm the VM name first \ - Export-VM / Checkpoint-VM before removing anything

destructive_patterns.name: remove-appxpackage
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-AppxPackage uninstalls an app package (potentially for all users).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-AppxPackage` uninstalls a Windows app package; with `-AllUsers` it removes it for \ everyone. Removing a provisioned/system app can break Windows features.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-AppxPackage: confirm the exact package first \ - Avoid -AllUsers unless you intend a machine-wide removal
